question: In public health statistics, what age limit is used to define an orphan?
explanation: Global health guidelines define an orphan as any child who has lost a parent before reaching their 18th birthday. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why are children whose parents are still alive sometimes counted when discussing HIV orphans and vulnerable children?

options.A: They always test positive for the virus at birth
options.B: They live in households where chronic illness severely drains resources
options.C: They possess legal custody over their sick parents
options.D: They are automatically placed in government orphanages

explanation: Even before parents pass away, chronic illness strips a household of income and makes daily survival a struggle. Great insight to keep in mind for community nursing! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h1)

question: What does 'role reversal' mean for a child affected by HIV in the family?

options.A: The child takes on adult caregiving and household responsibilities
options.B: The community rejects the child and adopts the parents instead
options.C: The child stops going to school to teach younger children
options.D: The child becomes the legal guardian of the extended family

explanation: Role reversal happens when a young child has to nurse sick adults or care for younger siblings, missing out on their own childhood. Spotting this helps nurses offer better support! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h2)

question: Why do many children affected by HIV face social isolation in their neighborhoods?

options.A: Mandatory quarantine laws enforced by local health workers
options.B: Fear of stigma and whispers linked to the family's HIV status
options.C: Complete lack of interest in making friends with other children
options.D: Government policies restricting them from public gatherings

explanation: Stigma creates a painful wall of fear and judgment, making families hide and children pull away from friends. Compassionate nursing care helps break down these barriers. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is a main reason why children affected by HIV often drop out of school?

options.A: Inability to pay for school fees, books, and uniforms
options.B: A national law banning orphans from attending public schools
options.C: Mandatory admission into vocational training centers
options.D: Constant medical quarantine inside local hospitals

explanation: When a breadwinner passes away, the family often faces severe financial hardship, making education costs impossible to cover. Education is key, and nurses advocate for these kids! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is a common misconception about the health status of HIV orphans?

options.A: People assume all orphans are infected with HIV themselves
options.B: People assume orphans never require routine immunizations
options.C: People think orphans are immune to childhood malnutrition
options.D: People believe orphans cannot contract malaria or typhoid

explanation: Not every child who loses a parent to HIV has the virus. Many are negative and simply suffering from poverty and loss. Keep this distinction clear in your practice! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h3)

question: In the context of vulnerable families, what is 'property grabbing'?

options.A: Community members stealing food donations meant for orphans
options.B: Relatives seizing land and belongings after a parent dies
options.C: The government confiscating hospital records of deceased patients
options.D: Banks freezing accounts belonging to children under age eighteen

explanation: Property grabbing happens when greedy relatives unlawfully chase away a grieving widow and her children to take over their home and properties. It's a harsh reality nurses should be aware of to guide families. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h4)

question: How does community stigma directly affect the wellbeing of an HIV orphan?

options.A: It guarantees the child free medical care in local clinics
options.B: It forces the government to build private housing for them
options.C: It improves their academic performance through strict discipline
options.D: It leads to social rejection, bullying, and isolation

explanation: Stigma cuts children off from vital community support systems, worsening their emotional pain and loneliness. Your friendly smile can make a huge difference to a patient! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h4)

question: During a home visit, what is a key sign of neglect that a community health nurse should look for?

options.A: Frequent attendance at youth club meetings
options.B: A high grade point average in primary school
options.C: Poor hygiene and delayed physical growth milestones

explanation: Physical signs like poor hygiene and stunted growth point directly to a lack of proper care, food, and supervision at home. Excellent assessment skill to master! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h5)

question: A community health nurse visits a home where a parent recently died from an AIDS-related illness. What is the best first step to take?

options.A: Discharge the family from clinic follow-up to protect patient privacy
options.B: Immediately report the extended family to the police for property grabbing
options.C: Transfer all children to a distant government orphanage home
options.D: Perform a comprehensive assessment of the children's nutritional and social needs

explanation: A complete nursing assessment helps you understand their health, feeding status, and immediate social needs so you can offer the right help. Nursing is all about holistic care! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why is putting a child in an orphanage usually considered a last resort?

options.A: Extended family members refuse to let children visit orphanages
options.B: Family-based care is better for a child's emotional development
options.C: Orphanages are illegal under Nigerian federal health laws
options.D: Institutions only accept children who are over eighteen years old

explanation: Children always thrive better emotionally and socially when raised within a family setting rather than an institution. Family love is powerful medicine! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the biggest challenge faced by child-headed households?

options.A: The government evicts them immediately for breaking zoning laws
options.B: Children lack adult guidance, financial stability, and legal protection
options.C: They are required by law to run community health clinics
options.D: They receive too much financial support from international donors

explanation: When young ones live alone without an adult, everyday survival becomes a massive struggle for food, shelter, and safety. Community nurses play a key role in identifying and helping them. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency coordinates national policies and responses related to HIV?
explanation: NACA is the main body responsible for coordinating the national fight against the HIV epidemic in Nigeria. Great exam fact to lock into your memory! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h7)

question: How do grassroots community programs directly help HIV orphans?

options.A: They provide localized support like food, school fees, and health checks
options.B: They construct massive industrial factories for child employment
options.C: They enforce mandatory DNA testing for all community members
options.D: They relocate every orphan outside of Nigeria to foreign countries

explanation: Grassroots programs bring practical, everyday assistance directly to the vulnerable children and families who need it most. You are doing brilliantly! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h7)
